name: the wash
human: A place people leave a car and walk away from for ten minutes.

name: the pumps
human: Somebody is always sitting in a car here not buying anything.

name: Engine 9
human: The doors are open in all weather and the crew watch the street from inside them.

name: the depot yard
human: Grass that grew because nobody got round to paving it.

name: the Hallam Building
human: Forty floors of offices and a lobby nobody is ever turned away from.

name: Northgate Elementary
human: Painted every summer and scuffed back to the undercoat by October.

name: Bruno's
human: Shut half the year, and the queue at Easter goes round the corner.

name: the public conveniences
human: Council-green tile and a door that does not lock.

name: the stand
human: Papers, cigarettes, and the man who knows who bought which.

name: Northgate Savings
human: Marble that was meant to look permanent.

name: the Northgate Diner
human: Open before anyone needs it to be, and the same four faces are in it at six.

name: the Meridian
human: A hundred and eleven metres of it, and the top four floors have been empty for a year.

name: Northgate General
human: The only lit windows on this street at four in the morning.

name: Franklin Park
human: Grass worn to earth along the line everyone actually walks.

name: Northgate Precinct
human: The light in the front office never goes off, which is not the same as somebody being awake.

name: the Rialto
human: Two screens, one of which has been showing the same film since spring.

name: the Regency Rooms
human: Open all night, and the carpet is loud enough that nobody notices the hour.

name: the precinct lot
human: Cruisers nose-in against the fence and everything else parked wherever.

name: the hospital lot
human: Full at visiting hours and never emptier than half.

name: behind the Regency
human: Nobody parks here who wants to be seen arriving.

name: the Savings lot
human: Painted bays, and everybody parks across two of them.

name: the school lot
human: Empty by four, apart from whoever is waiting.

name: Westway at Northway
human: The last block before the ring road, and half of it is still hoardings.

name: Market at Northway
human: Wholesalers, and nothing open after six.

name: First at Northway
human: The good end of the north side, which is not saying a great deal.

name: Second at Northway
human: Offices above, and a shop below that has been three different shops this year.

name: Third at Northway
human: Where the buses turn round.

name: Fourth at Northway
human: Backs onto the ring road and gets the noise of it all night.

name: Westway at Bishop
human: Rooming houses. Nobody signs a lease here for a year.

name: Third at Bishop
human: Trade counters, and a yard nobody locks.

name: Fourth at Bishop
human: The far side, and the streetlights on it have been out since spring.

name: Westway at Northgate
human: Cheap frontage on an expensive street, which tells you what happened here.

name: Third at Northgate
human: Two floors of anything and a top floor of nothing.

name: Fourth at Northgate
human: You can see the fields from the upper windows.

name: Westway at Franklin
human: The laundry, the pawn shop and the place that cashes cheques.

name: Third at Franklin
human: Quiet in a way the middle of town never is.

name: Fourth at Franklin
human: Half-let, and the half that is let keeps odd hours.

name: Westway at Hale
human: Built all at once and all the same, and it has not aged evenly.

name: Market at Hale
human: The south-west corner, and the wind comes straight up it.

name: First at Hale
human: Where people live who work in the middle.

name: Second at Hale
human: Shopfronts with flats over them and a bar at the end.

name: Third at Hale
human: Somebody keeps a light on all night on the third floor.

name: Fourth at Hale
human: The edge of it. After this there are fields.

name: Westway at Merrow
human: The southern limit, and it looks it.

name: Market at Merrow
human: Lock-ups, mostly. A few of them are not lock-ups.

name: First at Merrow
human: Terraces facing the ring road with their backs to each other.

name: Second at Merrow
human: A block you could park on all night and nobody would ask.

name: Third at Merrow
human: The last of the paving, and the kerbs give out halfway along.

name: Fourth at Merrow
human: The corner nobody has any reason to come to.

name: Beechwood Rise
human: Built all at once in the good year, and every third house has the same door.

name: The Larches
human: Nobody has cut down the tree it was named after, which is something.

name: Coronation Avenue
human: Bunting in the summer and nothing at all the rest of the year.

name: Northbound Gardens
human: Backs onto the ring road, and they all put the shed at that end.

name: Elm Grove
human: Dutch elm took the elms in the seventies and the name stayed.

name: Priory Close
human: There was never a priory. There was a man selling houses.

name: Kingfisher Way
human: The stream it is named for runs in a pipe under the third garden.

name: The Paddocks
human: It was, until nineteen sixty-eight.

name: Willow Bank
human: The gardens flood at the bottom and everybody planted willows about it.

name: Hawthorn Drive
human: A cul-de-sac, so the only cars on it belong to somebody who lives there.

name: Saint Cuthbert's Park
human: The church sold the glebe and this is what went on it.

name: Meadow Vale
human: Neither a meadow nor a vale, and the estate agent knew it.

name: Chestnut Avenue
human: Wide enough for two cars to pass, which on this side of town is a boast.

name: Sycamore Close
human: Somebody keeps a boat on a trailer here and has never once moved it.

name: The Beeches
human: Bay windows, and net curtains in every one of them.

name: Fairfield Road
human: The long way round to everywhere, which is why it is quiet.

name: Orchard Way
human: Built on one. Two of the old apple trees are still in back gardens.

name: Cedar Crescent
human: It curves for no reason anybody can now remember.

name: Lavender Hill
human: It is not a hill either.

name: Rowan Court
human: The newest of them, and the gardens have not grown into themselves yet.

name: Southbound Gardens
human: The corner plot has a caravan on it and has had for eleven years.

name: Mill Race
human: Named after a watercourse three miles away.

name: Apple Tree Lane
human: A lane once. It has kerbs and a turning head now.

name: Greenacres
human: Somebody has painted their front door a colour the rest have opinions about.

name: Hillside Close
human: You can see the fields from the upstairs back windows.

name: The Spinney
human: Two rows of houses and the last of the wood behind them.

name: Fern Bank
human: The quiet end, and the streetlight outside number twelve has been out since spring.

name: Woodland Rise
human: The last of it. After this there are fields.

name: Home Farm
human: The kitchen light is on at half past four and the radio is never off.

name: the yard
human: Mud, diesel and forty years of things that might come in useful.

name: the big barn
human: Big enough to lose a car in, and dark enough at noon that you would.

name: the near silo
human: It booms when you knock on it.

name: the far silo
human: Empty since the wet year, and the ladder up the side is still sound.

name: the near paddock
human: Cropped flat and empty. The gate has been open for a while.

name: the far paddock
human: You cannot see this one from the road, or the road from it.

name: the top field
human: Forty acres, and the tractor lines run out of true where the ground dips.

name: the long field
human: It floods at the bottom corner every spring and nobody has ever drained it.

name: the bottom field
human: The corn is over head height by August and the rows run away from the track.

name: the orchard
human: Planted in rows by somebody who is dead now.

name: the far acre
human: The last field before the road, and the one nobody bothers to walk.

name: the west belt
human: Planted as a windbreak and never thinned. You cannot see through it.

name: the west belt, middle
human: The stretch between the two roads, and the darkest of the three.

name: the west belt, south
human: It gives out where the ground turns wet.

name: the west belt, end
human: Somebody has been cutting firewood out of this one.

name: Wicker End
human: Nobody has farmed it for years. Somebody is living in it.

name: the old barn
human: Half the roof is down and the half that is not is worse.

name: the old orchard
human: Gone to scrub. The fruit falls and nobody picks it up.

name: the far spinney
human: Too small to be worth clearing and too thick to walk through quickly.

name: the far field
human: Nobody watches this one from anywhere.

name: the top of the hill
human: It catches the weather first and everything here is a week behind.

name: the middle field
human: Split by a hedge somebody grubbed out and never finished.

name: the east wood
human: Older than the town, and the boundary bank round it is older still.

name: the east wood, lower
human: The same wood, on the other side of the road that was put through it.

name: the long acre
human: Fenced for horses that were sold years ago.

name: the cross on the Bishop road
human: Somebody replaces the flowers. Nobody has ever been seen doing it.

name: the cross at the county line
human: It has been there longer than the road surface it stands on.

name: the high seat
human: A platform over the long field. Whoever built it did not build it for deer.

name: the seat above Wicker End
human: It looks at the orchard and at the back of the house, which is a choice.

name: the pitch in the east wood
human: The fire is out. How long it has been out is the question.

name: the far pitch
human: A bedroll, a case left open, and no track in or out that anybody has found.

name: Vance & Son
human: Ironmongery, and a man who can find the one screw you need in a minute.

name: the corner grocer
human: Everything a fortnight from its date and nobody has ever complained.

name: Meacham's
human: A tailor who has outlived three fashions and expects to outlive a fourth.

name: the chemist
human: The window has not changed since the coronation and neither has the smell.

name: the Weighhouse
human: Four o'clock and the same men are in it who were in it at noon.

name: Northgate Post Office
human: A queue that moves at the speed of one conversation at a time.

name: Ellery's
human: Open at five, which is either a service or an accusation.

name: the Fourth Street market
human: Fruit stacked to a geometry that survives being sold from.

name: Halliwell's
human: A general store, which out here means it stocks what the last person asked for.

name: the west bakery
human: Sells out by ten and does not bake more, on principle.

name: the Drovers
human: The car park is bigger than the pub and on Fridays it is not big enough.

name: the west common
human: Cut twice a year whether it needs it or not.

name: the Bishop road swings
human: One swing has been chained up since April and nobody remembers why.

name: the paper shop
human: Papers, sweets, and a bell that has never once been oiled.

name: Trewin's
human: A hardware shop that also does keys, shoes, and advice.

name: the west allotments
human: Thirty plots, four of them worked properly and the rest an argument.

name: the old burial ground
human: Older than anything still standing, and the names have gone off the stones.

name: the east grocer
human: Run by a family who have never agreed on the opening hours.

name: Ottery's
human: Wool, thread, and a cat that is not for sale.

name: the east bakery
human: The smell reaches the county line on a west wind.

name: the Wheatsheaf
human: Older than the road, and it shows in the floor.

name: the Wicker End rooms
human: Bingo, inquests, and the annual meeting about the verge.

name: the east common
human: A cricket square somebody still rolls.

name: the county line swings
human: The roundabout goes faster than it should and always has.

name: the county stores
human: The last shop before the county line and it knows it.

name: the east sub-office
human: One window, one clerk, and a scale that has been condemned twice.

name: the east allotments
human: Sheds built from doors, and every one of them locked.

name: the north dairy
human: Milk, eggs, and a slate for people who are good for it.

name: Kerrow's
human: A greengrocer who tells you what not to buy this week.

name: the north hardware
human: Paint mixed by eye and it has never once been wrong.

name: the Northway Arms
human: The first pub on the road in and the last one out.

name: the Northway swings
human: Gravel, which everybody agrees was a mistake.

name: the south grocer
human: Open latest of any of them, which is not saying much.

name: Lanyon's
human: A fishmonger a very long way from any sea.

name: the south chemist
human: The only one that opens on a Sunday, and only until eleven.

name: the Plough
human: A back room that is booked every night of the week by somebody.

name: the south rooms
human: Scout hut, polling station, and where the inquest was held.

name: the south allotments
human: The best soil in Northgate and everybody knows it.
